About.title: About
About.heroTitle: Atlasbot — knowledge and parts for AMR/AGV robots
About.heroSubtitle: From real projects to shared knowledge and field-tested parts — everything on Atlasbot starts with actually building and running real robots.
About.storyParagraph1: Atlasbot grew out of a very practical need: while building autonomous mobile robots (AMR) — from a differential-drive robot and a Mecanum robot to Atlas A2 running on a Jetson Orin Nano — every step meant hunting through scattered documentation, trial-and-error with parts of unknown quality, and rebuilding foundational knowledge from scratch, since good AMR/AGV material in Vietnamese was hard to find.
About.storyParagraph2: Atlasbot exists to fix exactly that: a systematic collection of technical knowledge, a showcase of real projects that actually run, and a curated set of parts based on hands-on experience from those same projects — instead of just reselling components that were never actually tested.
About.storyParagraph3: Beyond sharing knowledge and selling parts, Atlasbot works directly alongside AMR/AGV projects — from student capstone and research projects to real-world deployments at companies rolling out autonomous mobile robots. Whether it's a school project or a production rollout, the approach stays the same: helping pick the right hardware configuration and providing hands-on technical support from idea to a robot that actually runs — not just selling a product and walking away.
About.pillarBlogDesc: 9 topics from foundational knowledge to advanced ROS2 Navigation, written in the order you'd actually learn them — no fluff.
About.pillarProjectsDesc: Mecanum robot, differential-drive robot, Atlas A2 — open source on GitHub, with demo videos and the full build process.
About.pillarShopDesc: Sensors, microcontrollers, motors, chassis, wheels, batteries — curated from real hands-on use, not components that were never field-tested.
About.visionText: Atlasbot is currently in an early stage — the blog and shop mainly serve students and individual engineers in Vietnam, while AMR/AGV project support for businesses is handled on a per-project basis. Orders and project support requests are both confirmed manually via Messenger/Zalo — online payment isn't supported yet. The longer-term goal is to grow into a wholesale distributor serving larger business customers and international markets.
